title: Why you should talk to strangers, with Gillian Sandstrom, PhD, and Jon Levy

sentences.en: The guy who takes tickets in the office parking garage.
sentences.zh: 办公区停车场里那个收停车费的伙计。

sentences.en: The colleague in another department who used to take a coffee break at the same time as you.
sentences.zh: 另一个部门里那个以前总和你同时去喝咖啡休息的同事。

sentences.en: The parents at monthly PTA meetings.
sentences.zh: 每月家校联合会会议上的那些家长。

sentences.en: The commuters you shared a subway car with every morning.
sentences.zh: 每天早晨和你同乘一节地铁的通勤族。

sentences.en: Remember them?
sentences.zh: 还记得他们吗？

sentences.en: Before the pandemic, these wide circles of acquaintances and strangers were the backdrop of our daily lives.
sentences.zh: 在大流行之前，这些形形色色的熟人和陌生人构成了我们日常生活的背景。

sentences.en: Familiar, comforting, something we took for granted.
sentences.zh: 熟悉、温馨，是我们习以为常的事物。

sentences.en: Over the past year, as many of us have lamented our physical separation from close friends and family, how many of us have thought about missing those casual connections?
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，我们中的许多人都为与亲密朋友和家人的物理隔离感到惋惜，又有多少人曾想过错过那些泛泛之交呢？

sentences.en: When's the last time you actually spoke to a stranger?
sentences.zh: 你上一次真正跟陌生人说话是什么时候？

sentences.en: And despite the fact that so many of us profess to dislike making small talk,
sentences.zh: 尽管我们当中有那么多人声称自己不喜欢闲聊，

sentences.en: it turns out that these kinds of connections and conversations actually strengthen our mental health and enrich our lives.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这类联系和对话实际上能够增强我们的心理健康，丰富我们的生活。

sentences.en: So what do we gain from meeting new people and chatting with strangers?
sentences.zh: 那么，结识新朋友和与陌生人闲聊能给我们带来什么？

sentences.en: What have we been missing out on this past year?
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，我们错失了什么？

sentences.en: And as life begins to go back to normal in the coming months, we hope, how can we become better at meeting new people and embracing the opportunity to talk to strangers?
sentences.zh: 随着未来几个月生活开始恢复正常（我们希望如此），我们该如何更好地结识新朋友并抓住与陌生人交谈的机会呢？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客节目，主要探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天请来了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: Dr. Jillian Sandstrom is a senior lecturer in psychology at the University of Essex in the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 吉莉安·桑德斯特罗姆博士是英国埃塞克斯大学心理学高级讲师。

sentences.en: She studies what she calls minimal social interactions and has found that despite many people's reluctance to talk to strangers,
sentences.zh: 她研究她所谓的“微型社交互动”，并发现尽管许多人排斥与陌生人交谈，

sentences.en: these interactions are usually enjoyable and actually are good for us.
sentences.zh: 但这些互动通常令人愉快，而且实际上对我们有益。

sentences.en: She's become an advocate for the benefits of talking to strangers, has spoken widely on the topic, and even developed a workshop called How to Talk to Strangers.
sentences.zh: 她已成为倡导与陌生人交谈益处的践行者，曾就此主题发表过多场演讲，甚至还开发了一个名为《如何与陌生人交谈》的工作坊。

sentences.en: Our second guest is John Levy, a consultant, writer, and speaker who has had a lot of opportunity to watch strangers talk to one another.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二位嘉宾是约翰·利维，他是一名顾问、作家和演讲者，有很多机会观察陌生人彼此交谈。

sentences.en: More than a decade ago, he founded what he calls the Influencers Dinner, regular gatherings that brought strangers together who are leaders in their fields,
sentences.zh: 十多年前，他创立了所谓的“影响者晚宴”，这是一个定期聚会，将各自领域的领军人物——

sentences.en: Olympic athletes, business executives, Nobel Prize winners, artists, musicians, and others,
sentences.zh: 奥运会运动员、企业高管、诺贝尔奖得主、艺术家、音乐家以及其他人——聚在一起，

sentences.en: to cook dinner and converse with each other without at first knowing any other guest's identity.
sentences.zh: 大家一起做饭、交流，起初并不知道其他客人的真实身份。

sentences.en: His book, You're Invited, The Art and Science of Cultivating Influence, will be released in May.
sentences.zh: 他的新书《承蒙盛情：培养影响力的艺术与科学》将于五月出版。

sentences.en: It talks about the importance of making human connections and building trust and community to accomplish our goals.
sentences.zh: 书中探讨了建立人际联系、构建信任和社群对于实现我们目标的重要性。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位今天做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: I think your different perspectives should make for a really interesting conversation.
sentences.zh: 我认为你们不同的视角一定会碰撞出非常有趣的对话。

sentences.en: Looking forward to our chat.
sentences.zh: 我很期待我们的交流。

sentences.en: I'm super excited to be here.
sentences.zh: 我特别高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: I'm dying to dive into like Jillian's research.
sentences.zh: 我迫不及待地想深入了解吉莉安的研究。

sentences.en: I can't wait to see what I can apply to my dinner parties and events.
sentences.zh: 我等不及要看看有哪些可以应用到我的晚宴和活动中了。

sentences.en: Well, we will get there.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们马上会聊到那些。

sentences.en: Let's start with you, Dr. Sandstrom.
sentences.zh: 我们先从您开始，桑德斯特罗姆博士。

sentences.en: As I mentioned in the introduction, you study minimal social interactions.
sentences.zh: 正如我在介绍中所提到的，您研究的是微型社交互动。

sentences.en: Can you define that?
sentences.zh: 您能下个定义吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think I'll answer that question by kind of giving my origin story or one of my origin stories.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想我可以通过讲述我的起源故事，或者说其中一个起源故事来回答这个问题。

sentences.en: So, when I started studying my master's degree, which I did at Ryerson University, which is right downtown Toronto in Canada.
sentences.zh: 当时我开始读硕士学位，是在瑞尔森大学读的，它就在加拿大安大略省多伦多市的市中心。

sentences.en: So, just right in the middle of the city.
sentences.zh: 也就是在城市的正中央。

sentences.en: And I would walk from the research lab to my supervisor's office.
sentences.zh: 我会从研究实验室步行到我导师的办公室。

sentences.en: And when I did that, I would pass a hot dog stand.
sentences.zh: 当我走那条路时，会路过一个热狗摊。

sentences.en: And I somehow, without meaning to, developed a relationship with the lady who worked at the hot dog stand.
sentences.zh: 不知怎么的，在无意之中，我和热狗摊工作的女士建立了一种联系。

sentences.en: And every day when I walked past her, I would smile and wave and she would wave back.
sentences.zh: 每天我从她身边走过时，都会对她微笑并挥手，她也会挥手回应。

sentences.en: And it just really made me feel good.
sentences.zh: 这真的让我感觉很好。

sentences.en: And so, I just started wondering, what's going on here?
sentences.zh: 于是我开始琢磨，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Is this just me or is this a thing?
sentences.zh: 这只是我个人的感受，还是普遍存在的现象？

sentences.en: And that's how I ended up doing this research.
sentences.zh: 这就是我最终开展这项研究的原因。

sentences.en: So, it started from there.
sentences.zh: 所以，一切就是从那里开始的。

sentences.en: And I guess I look at the kind of relationships that we have that, at least when I started, I was looking at what I call weak ties, which is kind of one step up from a stranger.
sentences.zh: 我想我所关注的是那种关系，至少在我刚开始的时候，我关注的是我所谓的“弱连接”，这比陌生人稍微进了一步。

sentences.en: You know, someone like the hot dog lady or the kind of people you mentioned during the intro.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像热狗摊的女士，或者你在引言中提到的那种人。

sentences.en: So, not strangers because there's mutual recognition.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不算陌生人，因为彼此认得。

sentences.en: So, I think that's the sort of, you know, tiny line between a stranger and a weak tie.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这就是陌生人和弱连接之间那条微小的界线。

sentences.en: But I've been more interested in the ones on the more minimal side than the acquaintances that we see on a regular basis and are actually quite close to.
sentences.zh: 但我更感兴趣的是那些偏向极简的互动，而不是我们经常见面且关系其实相当亲密的熟人。

sentences.en: So, I think that the word acquaintance can be really, really broad.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为“熟人”这个词可以非常非常广泛。

sentences.en: It encompasses a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 它涵盖了很多人。

sentences.en: And I've been more interested on the more minimal side.
sentences.zh: 而我更关注那些偏向极简的互动。

sentences.en: So, a lot of your research has found that people worry about talking to strangers.
sentences.zh: 因此，你的许多研究发现，人们对与陌生人交谈感到担忧。

sentences.en: We all are a little uncomfortable with the idea.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人对这个想法都感到有些不自在。

sentences.en: We don't think that they'll enjoy it or that the other person will enjoy being talked to.
sentences.zh: 我们认为他们不会乐意，或者对方会觉得跟人交谈很扫兴。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Are these worries valid?
sentences.zh: 这些担忧成立吗？

sentences.en: Well, the easy answer to that second part is no, they are not.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对第二部分那个问题的简单回答是：不，并不成立。

sentences.en: I mean, they're not accurate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们并不准确。

sentences.en: Maybe it makes sense that we have them.
sentences.zh: 也许我们产生这些担忧是合情合理的。

sentences.en: And yeah, my research has found, you know, over the last 10 years, I've been doing this research and I've done lots of different studies.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的研究发现，在过去的10年里，我一直在做这项研究，做过许多不同的研究。

sentences.en: And I find people are just worried about so many different things.
sentences.zh: 我发现人们只是在担心各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: So, they're worried about how they're going to feel about the conversation and whether they have the skills to maintain the conversation.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们担心自己对这场对话会有什么感觉，以及自己是否有能力维持对话。

sentences.en: But they're also equally worried about their conversation partner.
sentences.zh: 但他们对谈话对象的担忧也同样不少。

sentences.en: Is that person going to like me?
sentences.zh: 那个人会喜欢我吗？

sentences.en: Are they going to want to talk to me?
sentences.zh: 他们会想跟我说话吗？

sentences.en: Are they going to be able to carry on this conversation?
sentences.zh: 他们能把这个对话进行下去吗？

sentences.en: Are we going to have one of those dreaded, awkward silences?
sentences.zh: 我们会出现那种让人畏惧的尴尬沉默吗？

sentences.en: So, yeah, generally speaking, people are quite worried about all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，总的来说，人们对各种事情都相当担忧。

sentences.en: But when you actually get them to have a conversation and report back afterwards, they kind of have to admit that none of those things they worried about really happened.
sentences.zh: 但当你真的让他们进行了一场对话并在事后反馈时，他们不得不承认，他们担心的那些事情根本没有发生。

sentences.en: And over and over again, I find that people enjoy their conversations much more than they expect to.
sentences.zh: 一次又一次，我发现人们比他们预期中要更加享受这些对话。

sentences.en: So, John, through your influencer dinners and now your influencer Zooms, you've had a lot of opportunity to watch strangers talk to each other.
sentences.zh: 那么，约翰，通过你的影响者晚宴，以及现在的线上影响者聚会，你有很多机会观察陌生人彼此交谈。

sentences.en: Tell us a little bit about these events and why you started this project.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲这些活动，以及你为什么会发起这个项目吧。

sentences.en: So, I was 28 years old, overweight, in debt, and literally like the poster child for not living up to your potential.
sentences.zh: 当时我28岁，超重，负债累累，简直就是“未能发挥潜能”的典型代表。

sentences.en: And I came across some research by Nicholas Christakis and James Fowler about the spread of obesity.
sentences.zh: 我偶然看到了尼古拉斯·克里斯塔基斯和詹姆斯·福勒关于肥胖传播的研究。
zh_words: 尼古拉斯·克里斯塔基斯

sentences.en: They were curious, does it spread like a cold from person to person or is it a percentage of the population?
sentences.zh: 他们很好奇，肥胖会像感冒一样在人与人之间传播，还是说它只占人口的一定比例？

sentences.en: And they found that if you have a friend who's obese, your probability of obesity increases by 45%.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，如果你有一个肥胖的朋友，你发胖的概率会增加45%。

sentences.en: Your friends who don't know them have a 20% increased chance and their friends have a 5% increased chance.
sentences.zh: 你不认识的朋友的朋友，其发胖几率会增加20%，而他们朋友的朋友发胖几率则会增加5%。

sentences.en: And so, I figured rather than beating myself up for not like wanting to set an alarm at 6 a.m.
sentences.zh: 因此我想，与其因为自己不想在早上6点定闹钟去锻炼而自责，

sentences.en: to work out, maybe I could get contagious behaviors like exercise or better financial habits just by getting to know people.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以通过了解他人，来获得具有传染性的行为，比如锻炼或更好的财务习惯。

sentences.en: And I realized that that would be compounded if I could get all these strangers that are really successful to know each other because then they could positively influence one another.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，如果我能让所有这些非常成功的陌生人彼此结识，这种效果将会倍增，因为这样他们就可以积极地互相影响。

sentences.en: And so, I started modeling their behavior and trying to figure out what they would want to engage with.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始模仿他们的行为，并试图找出他们愿意参与的内容。

sentences.en: And I realized that it needs to be something novel and there are a few other characteristics.
sentences.zh: 我意识到这必须是新颖的，而且还有其他一些特征。

sentences.en: And so, I think, Jillian, you've probably seen this in your work as well.
sentences.zh: 我想，吉莉安，你可能在你的工作中也见过这种情况。

sentences.en: Well, there's this weird characteristics that we all have called the IKEA effect,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们所有人身上都有一个奇怪的特征，叫做“宜家效应”，

sentences.en: which states that we disproportionately care about our IKEA furniture because we had to assemble it.
sentences.zh: 它指出我们对自己的宜家家具格外在意，因为那是我们自己组装的。

sentences.en: So, because of this ridiculous trait that when we invest effort into something, we care about it more.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于这种荒谬的特质——当我们对某事投入了精力时，我们就会更加在乎它。

sentences.en: I realized I was going to invite people to do something together.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我要邀请人们一起做点什么。

sentences.en: And I ended up falling on cooking a meal.
sentences.zh: 最后我落脚于做一顿饭。

sentences.en: And the big joke is that after a bunch of these dinners, it was probably like five, six years in, we had a famous journalist come and she said,
sentences.zh: 最好笑的是，在举办了这么多次晚宴之后，大概是五六年的时候，我们来了一位著名的记者，她说：

sentences.en: I was expecting a phenomenal meal and decent company.
sentences.zh: “我本以为会有一顿惊艳的饭菜和还不错的陪伴。”

sentences.en: I got the exact opposite.
sentences.zh: “结果却恰恰相反。”

sentences.en: So, it's terrible.
sentences.zh: 所以，这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Like, the meals are awful.
sentences.zh: 就像，饭菜很难吃。

sentences.en: Like, I mean, they're fine, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，其实还行吧？

sentences.en: But go to Chipotle, you'll have a better meal.
sentences.zh: 但你去墨西哥快餐店，能吃到更好的饭菜。

sentences.en: But what I found is that, and the research, I believe, really supports this,
sentences.zh: 但我发现的是——我相信研究也非常支持这一点——

sentences.en: is that a shared activity functions as a social catalyst that eliminates a lot of the awkwardness and concern.
sentences.zh: 共同参与一项活动可以起到社交催化剂的作用，消除了许多尴尬和顾虑。

sentences.en: So, if I ask people to move a table or chop some vegetables, conversation actually flows much faster and more naturally.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我请大家搬一张桌子或切点蔬菜，对话的进行实际上会快得多，也自然得多。

sentences.en: Does that ring true for you, Jillian?
sentences.zh: 吉莉安，这听起来对你来说感同身受吗？

sentences.en: Is that what you see in your research too?
sentences.zh: 这跟你从研究中看到的一样吗？

sentences.en: I mean, just speaking from personal experience, I mean, I get asked a lot about tips for starting a conversation.
sentences.zh: 我是说，仅从个人经验来讲，经常有人向我讨教开启对话的小贴士。

sentences.en: And I mean, basically, what you're talking about, John, is sort of a built-in conversation starter.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，约翰，你刚才谈到的基本上就是一种内置的破冰话题。

sentences.en: And everybody there has something in common because they've all chosen to take you up on this, you know, crazy, somewhat crazy endeavor.
sentences.zh: 在那里的每个人都有共同点，因为他们都选择接受了你这个疯狂的、多少有点疯狂的尝试。

sentences.en: So, in some ways, they're sort of built-in things that would make it easier to talk.
sentences.zh: 所以在某些方面，有一些内置的因素会让交谈变得更容易。

sentences.en: But I'm curious to ask you a question.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇想问你一个问题。

sentences.en: Like, do you sometimes see people worrying about the conversation?
sentences.zh: 比如，你有时会看到人们对对话感到担忧吗？

sentences.en: Because even, you know, even the kinds of people that you're inviting, surely there's some among them that are less extroverted and more sort of socially anxious.
sentences.zh: 因为哪怕，你知道的，哪怕是你邀请的那类人，其中肯定也有一些不太外向、社交焦虑较多的人。

sentences.en: And so, I'm curious if you see that kind of fears that I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇你是否也见到了我所说的那种恐惧。

sentences.en: Oh, without a doubt.
sentences.zh: 哦，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: I think that you're spot on with everything that you've said, both the concern.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你说的每一句话都切中要害，包括那些顾虑。

sentences.en: And there's actually a secondary concern.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上还有第二层顾虑。

sentences.en: Because they're coming into the home of a stranger, about like 15 minutes in, the first part we do kind of like cocktails, maybe show people the house that they're in.
sentences.zh: 因为他们是走进一个陌生人的家，大约在15分钟后，我们进行的第一部分类似于鸡尾酒会，可能会带大家参观他们所在的房子。

sentences.en: But after about 15 minutes in, once like people have relaxed a little, they'll say, oh, I'm so sorry.
sentences.zh: 但在大约15分钟后，一旦人们稍微放松下来，他们就会说：哦，实在不好意思。

sentences.en: I just have to call my spouse and let them know that I still have both of my kidneys.
sentences.zh: 我得给配偶打个电话，让他们知道我还长着两个肾。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I haven't been kidnapped.
sentences.zh: 就像我没有被绑架一样。

sentences.en: This isn't some like organ scam.
sentences.zh: 这不是什么器官贩卖的骗局。

sentences.en: And that's probably like less of a concern when you're on this, like, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 当你坐在，我不知道，

sentences.en: a bus and you're not worried that the person who turns to you and asks you about the book you're reading is after your kidneys.
sentences.zh: 一辆公交车上时，这种顾虑可能就没那么大，你不会担心那个转过身来向你询问你正在看的书的人是冲着你的肾来的。

sentences.en: Well, funny enough, though, like when I talk to someone on the bus, I actually assume that there's sort of these three stages that people are going through.
sentences.zh: 说来有趣，当我在公交车上和某人说话时，我实际上认为人们会经历这大约三个阶段。

sentences.en: And this is not something I've actually tested.
sentences.zh: 这不是我实际验证过的东西。

sentences.en: But I assume that people's first thought is, you know, do I know you?
sentences.zh: 但我猜测人们的第一想法是，你知道的，我认识你吗？

sentences.en: Because, you know, people don't just talk to each other that often.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，人们不会无缘无故经常互相搭话。

sentences.en: So they think, well, you know, if you're talking to me, you must have a reason for it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会想，好吧，如果你在跟我说话，你肯定有原因。

sentences.en: And so the first thought is, you know, maybe I know you.
sentences.zh: 因此第一反应是，也许我认识你。

sentences.en: And once they realize, oh, I don't know you, then they do start to worry.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们意识到，哦，我不认识你，接着他们就开始担心了。

sentences.en: I think they think, you know, you must be trying to get something.
sentences.zh: 我想他们会觉得，你一定是有所图谋。

sentences.en: Maybe you're trying to sell something or maybe, you know, you're crazy or maybe like maybe you do want to harm them.
sentences.zh: 也许你想推销什么，或者也许你脑子有毛病，或者也许你真的想伤害他们。

sentences.en: And then I think, you know, if you have to persist a little bit and get to the point where people realize you're just being friendly and you just want to have a chat.
sentences.zh: 然后我觉得，如果你必须坚持一会儿，达到让人们意识到你只是在释放友好、只想聊聊天的地步。

sentences.en: And if you can get to that point, then you're golden.
sentences.zh: 如果你能达到那个点，那就万事大吉了。

sentences.en: But sometimes, you know, it can take longer with some people to get to that point.
sentences.zh: 但有时，你知道的，对某些人来说，可能需要更长时间才能达到那个阶段。

sentences.en: And some people will never be able to get there because they just have too much anxiety and get stuck on, stuck in the middle somewhere.
sentences.zh: 有些人永远也到不了那个阶段，因为他们的焦虑太重了，卡在了中间的某个地方。

sentences.en: So I'm super curious about something.
sentences.zh: 所以我对一件事超级好奇。

sentences.en: It seems that that in general, anxiety and concern has increased over the past, let's say, 30, 40 years in terms of our safety.
sentences.zh: 似乎在过去，比方说30、40年里，就我们的安全而言，总体的焦虑和担忧有所增加。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So according to most statistics, we're in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以根据大多数统计数据，我们在美国，

sentences.en: at least safer in just about every way.
sentences.zh: 几乎在各方面都更安全。

sentences.en: But there's this rise of helicopter parenting and like this fear of talking to strangers over the past 10 years.
sentences.zh: 但在过去10年里，出现了过度保护式的育儿方式，以及对与陌生人交谈的恐惧。

sentences.en: Have you seen that there's greater concern or do you think it's kind of stayed about the same?
sentences.zh: 你觉得人们的担忧加剧了，还是觉得它基本保持不变？

sentences.en: I mean, as a psychologist, I don't tend to do the sort of studying things over time and looking at the history of it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为一名心理学家，我通常不会做那种随着时间推移研究事物并审视其历史的工作。

sentences.en: I'd love to to work with someone on those kind of questions.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意与研究这类问题的人合作。

sentences.en: But I mean, I'm I think, you know, I don't want to be blaming social media for all of the world's problems because that's doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，我——我不想把世界上所有的问题都归咎于社交媒体，因为那毫无意义。

sentences.en: But I think young people especially can use social media and use their phones to sort of avoid having too much face to face interaction with people.
sentences.zh: 但我认为年轻人尤其会利用社交媒体和手机来避免与他人进行太多的面对面互动。

sentences.en: And if you don't have that practice to build up the skills, then it could you could build it up in your head as something that's really fearful.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有进行这种练习来培养技能，那么你可能会在脑海中把它想象成一件非常可怕的事情。

sentences.en: And then because you don't have a lot of practice, you try it.
sentences.zh: 然后因为你缺乏练习，你决定试一试。

sentences.en: It doesn't go so well.
sentences.zh: 结果并不太顺利。

sentences.en: And then you start to think, I don't have the skills to do this.
sentences.zh: 接着你开始想，我根本没有能力做好这件事。

sentences.en: And then it becomes even scarier and you get into this sort of negative cycle.
sentences.zh: 于是它变得更加可怕，你陷入了这种负面循环之中。

sentences.en: So I suspect that and, you know, not just not just talking about young people, but, you know, the world is sort of set up.
sentences.zh: 所以我怀疑，而且，你知道的，不仅仅是年轻人，整个世界似乎也是这样构成的。

sentences.en: We're trying to make things more and more efficient.
sentences.zh: 我们试图让事情变得越来越高效。

sentences.en: And we're factoring out a lot of the opportunities for social interaction.
sentences.zh: 而我们正在剔除大量社交互动的机会。

sentences.en: You know, there was an article in the news recently about how, you know, there's going to be a new grocery store that has no human checkouts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，最近新闻里有一篇文章报道说，将要出现一家没有人工收银台的新杂货店。

sentences.en: Like everybody just sort of swipes and walks out the door and, you know, like we're doing these kind of things for certain reasons, but, you know,
sentences.zh: 就像每个人都只是刷一下卡然后走出大门，你知道的，我们出于某些原因在做这些事，但是，

sentences.en: it has these negative consequences, which is taking away some of this human contact.
sentences.zh: 它带来了这些负面后果，那就是剥夺了部分人与人之间的接触。

sentences.en: And I don't know, I think especially right now with the pandemic, I hope it reminds us that we're all kind of because we're all going through this crazy thing together.
sentences.zh: 而且我不知道，我觉得特别是现在经历了这场大流行，我希望它能提醒我们，因为我们都在共同经历这件疯狂的事。

sentences.en: I hope it reminds us of our common humanity and makes people value that human contact, even with people that they don't know or don't know well.
sentences.zh: 我希望这能提醒我们共同的人性，让人类珍视这种人际交往，哪怕是对那些不认识或不够熟悉的人。

sentences.en: I think that that's super interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这超级有趣。

sentences.en: And my big concern is since my entire life is about bringing people together and giving them a sense of belonging,
sentences.zh: 而我最大的担忧是，既然我的整个生活都在于把人们聚集在一起并赋予他们归属感，

sentences.en: it seems that those people who already feel lonely fall into the loop of feeling like they're deserving to be lonely.
sentences.zh: 那些原本就感到孤独的人似乎会陷入一种觉得自己活该孤独的怪圈。

sentences.en: And so as we try to start now come out of this pandemic and more vaccines are available and we are seeing rates decrease of infection,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们试图开始走出这场大流行，有更多疫苗可用，且感染率正在下降时，

sentences.en: my concern is that there'll be a whole collection of people who are moving towards the roaring 20s and then a whole lot of people who will feel more isolated than ever.
sentences.zh: 我担心会出现这样一群人，他们正迈向狂欢的二十年代，而另一大群人则会感到前所未有的孤立。

sentences.en: And if we look back as far as 1985, the average American had just about three close friends besides family.
sentences.zh: 如果我们回溯到1985年，普通美国人除了家人之外，大约只有三个密友。

sentences.en: By 2004, that was down to just about two.
sentences.zh: 到2004年，这个数字下降到了大约两个。

sentences.en: I think it was the University of Chicago study.
sentences.zh: 我想那是芝加哥大学的一项研究。

sentences.en: And my concern around that is that the reason for it wasn't social media.
sentences.zh: 我对此的担忧在于，造成这一现象的原因并不是社交媒体。

sentences.en: It wasn't anything that we currently blame.
sentences.zh: 也不是我们目前归咎的任何其他因素。

sentences.en: It was more likely that people moved away from their family after college for work.
sentences.zh: 更有可能是人们在大学毕业后为了工作而搬离了家人身边。

sentences.en: And so we've set up a very mobile society where social ties are.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们建立了一个高度流动性的社会，在这个社会中，社交纽带……

sentences.en: It becomes acceptable to let them go for the progress, kind of like you said, of, you know, the faster checkout line, the bigger promotion, the bigger office.
sentences.zh: 为了进步而选择放手变得可以接受，有点像你说的，为了更快的结账通道、更大的晋升、更大的办公室。

sentences.en: But at a pretty significant expense.
sentences.zh: 但代价相当沉重。

sentences.en: And so I really hope that we can all learn how to like apply your research, because I think it would be great to be able to safely talk to strangers again.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的希望我们都能学会如何应用你的研究，因为我觉得能够再次安全地与陌生人交谈会是一件很棒的事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So let's talk for a minute, Jillian, about the mental health benefits to these casual interactions and conversations.
sentences.zh: 吉莉安，那我们花几分钟来聊聊这些日常互动和对话对心理健康的好处吧。

sentences.en: What have you found specifically?
sentences.zh: 你具体发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the first study I ran, which I did as part of my PhD, I ran at Starbucks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我开展的第一项研究是我在攻读博士学位期间在星巴克做的。

sentences.en: So I just stopped people on the street and asked them if they would help out with the research study in exchange for a Starbucks gift card.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是在街上拦住人们，问他们是否愿意配合一项研究，报酬是一张星巴克礼品卡。

sentences.en: So they had to go into Starbucks right then and there.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须当时就走进星巴克。

sentences.en: And the only catch was that they had to follow some instructions when they went in.
sentences.zh: 唯一的条件是他们在进去的时候必须遵循一些指示。

sentences.en: And so we asked some people to just be as efficient as possible to have their money ready and avoid unnecessary conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们要求一些人尽可能高效，准备好钱，避免不必要的对话。

sentences.en: We tried to tell them, you know, this this will be a good thing for the people working there because they just want to get through their shift.
sentences.zh: 我们试着告诉他们，这对那里工作的人来说是件好事，因为他们只想熬过这个班次。

sentences.en: And but then other people, we said, when you buy your coffee, try and turn it into a real social interaction.
sentences.zh: 但对于另一些人，我们说，当你买咖啡时，尽量把它变成一次真正的社交互动。

sentences.en: Smile, make eye contact, have a little chat.
sentences.zh: 微笑，有眼神交流，简单聊几句。

sentences.en: And lots of people said, oh, yeah, I do that all the time.
sentences.zh: 很多人说，哦，对啊，我一直都这么做。

sentences.en: And I said, OK, try to do it a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 我说，好的，那就试着再多做一点。

sentences.en: But when people came out with their coffee, what we found is that the people who had had that little chat,
sentences.zh: 但当人们拿着咖啡出来时，我们发现，那些有过简短聊天的人——

sentences.en: who turned that sort of everyday conversation that you might not even notice into something a little bit more social,
sentences.zh: 把那种你可能甚至不会注意到的日常对话变成了一点点更具社交性的交流的人——

sentences.en: they were in a better mood and felt more connected to other people.
sentences.zh: 他们的心情更好，并且感觉与他人的联系更紧密。

sentences.en: So those are the two findings that come up over and over again in my research and other people's research is just these moods,
sentences.zh: 这就是我的研究以及其他人的研究中一再出现的两个发现，即情绪上的好处、

sentences.en: sort of well-being benefits and this sense of connection to other people.
sentences.zh: 某种幸福感的提升，以及与他人产生这种连接感。

sentences.en: Research showed that we'd interact with anywhere from 11 to 16 people per day whom we didn't know very well.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，我们每天会与大约11到16个不太熟悉的人进行互动。

sentences.en: And nowadays, I would venture to say most of us don't see any strangers for days on end.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我敢说我们大多数人连续好几天都见不到一个陌生人。

sentences.en: Some social scientists have dubbed this turtling up.
sentences.zh: 一些社会学家把这称为“缩头乌龟式生存”。

sentences.en: I really like that term.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢这个词。

sentences.en: Are you concerned?
sentences.zh: 你担心吗？

sentences.en: Is this going to have a long term negative effect on people, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为这会对人们产生长期的负面影响吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that remains to be seen, of course.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这当然还有待观察。

sentences.en: I think it could go either way.
sentences.zh: 我认为结果可能会走向任何一个方向。

sentences.en: And like John said, it might go different ways for different people.
sentences.zh: 正如约翰所说，对不同的人来说，结果可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: I mean, I hope that a lot of people will start, well, because of the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我希望很多人会开始，嗯，因为这场大流行，

sentences.en: have started to realize that it's not just the close friends and family who they probably have managed to stay in touch with throughout the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 已经开始意识到，不仅仅是那些可能在整个大流行期间设法保持联系的密友和家人，

sentences.en: It's, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: all these other people in our lives really do matter and hopefully we're noticing that and we're missing them and we're realizing that maybe we should spend more time building up those relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们生活中的所有其他人其实也同样重要，希望我们能注意到这一点，开始想念他们，并意识到也许我们应该花更多时间去建立这些关系。

sentences.en: So to the extent that that happens, you know, hopefully when we have more freedom of movement and freedom to be with other people,
sentences.zh: 因此，在某种程度上，你知道的，希望当我们有更多行动自由和与他人相处的自由时，

sentences.en: that people will sort of make even more efforts than they ever have to sort of build those relationships.
sentences.zh: 人们会比以往任何时候都更加努力地去建立这些关系。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, you know, we were talking earlier about social anxiety a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但从另一方面来看，你知道的，我们刚才稍微聊了一下社交焦虑。

sentences.en: Some people might, you know, we've just spent the last year basically being told that we should be scared of other people or we could interpret it that way.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会，你知道的，我们在过去的一年里基本上一直被告知我们应该害怕其他人，或者我们可以这样解读它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, you know, it's hard to shake that off.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这很难摆脱。

sentences.en: I mean, I know myself, like during the first, you know, first month or so of the pandemic, there's a park across the street for me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我自己也知道，比如在大流行的头一个月左右，我街对面有一个公园。

sentences.en: And the best thing for my sanity is to go for a walk, which I do almost every day, just get some fresh air.
sentences.zh: 保持精神健康的最佳方式就是去散步，我几乎每天都去，呼吸点新鲜空气。

sentences.en: And also it's a chance to see other human beings.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个见到其他人类的机会。

sentences.en: But I remember the first couple of weeks of the first lockdown, I was just feeling really nervous.
sentences.zh: 但我记得第一次封锁的前几周，我真的感到很紧张。

sentences.en: You know, other people are possibly contagious and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，其他人可能是传染源并且很危险。

sentences.en: And so, you know, if they were standing to walking too close to me, like I just didn't want to be anywhere near them.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，如果他们站在或走到离我很近的地方，我根本不想靠近他们。

sentences.en: I didn't even look at other people.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不看其他人一眼。

sentences.en: And then I realized, you know, this is an over the top reaction.
sentences.zh: 然后我意识到，这是一种过激的反应。

sentences.en: I can still keep a safe distance, but still smile and, you know, acknowledge other humans and our shared humanity.
sentences.zh: 我仍然可以保持安全的距离，但同时微笑，你知道的，承认其他人类以及我们共同的人性。

sentences.en: And I can probably make a difference to everybody's feeling really anxious.
sentences.zh: 而且我或许可以对那些感到非常焦虑的人产生影响。

sentences.en: I could maybe help people by just being friendly and, you know, trying to, again, like demonstrate this fellow humanity.
sentences.zh: 我可以通过表现得友善来帮助人们，你知道的，再次尝试展现这种同理心。

sentences.en: It makes people feel good.
sentences.zh: 这让人感觉很好。

sentences.en: It makes me feel good.
sentences.zh: 这也让我感觉很好。

sentences.en: If someone, you know, smiles at me in the park when I'm in a bad mood, it changes my day.
sentences.zh: 如果有人在公园里对我微笑，而我当时心情不好，这会改变我的一整天。

sentences.en: So I hope that I can do that for other people too.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望我也能为其他人这样做。

sentences.en: So I think, you know, we don't have to be scared,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，你知道的，我们不必害怕，

sentences.en: but there has been a lot of fear over the last year and it would be easy for that to turn into a sustained kind of nervousness about interacting with other people and then have this negative cycle where,
sentences.zh: 但在过去的一年里确实存在很多恐惧，而这种恐惧很容易变成一种对与他人互动持续的紧张感，进而导致这样的负面循环：

sentences.en: you know, we're out of practice.
sentences.zh: 我们疏于练习。

sentences.en: So we feel that we're not any good at it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们觉得自己不擅长这个。

sentences.en: So we don't do it.
sentences.zh: 于是我们就不去做。

sentences.en: So we get even more out of practice.
sentences.zh: 结果我们变得更加生疏。

sentences.en: So I think that's the problem is that, you know, there could be this sort of downward spiral that makes it really difficult for people.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得问题就在于，可能会出现这种恶性循环，给人们带来极大的困难。

sentences.en: So, John, you're coming at this from a different perspective.
sentences.zh: 所以，约翰，你是从一个不同的角度来看待这个问题的。

sentences.en: You've thought a lot about how meeting new people can help build networks and accomplish goals.
sentences.zh: 你一直在深入思考结识新朋友如何帮助建立人脉并实现目标。

sentences.en: Is that why most people go to your events, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为这就是大多数人来参加你的活动的原因吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think that they just want to meet new people and that there is some interest in, you know, saying hello to strangers?
sentences.zh: 还是你觉得他们只是想结识新朋友，并且对向陌生人问好有某种兴趣？

sentences.en: I think that there's a handful of reasons that people come to my events.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们来参加我的活动有几个原因。

sentences.en: We've really built it around four or five characteristics.
sentences.zh: 我们确实是围绕四五个特点来构建活动的。

sentences.en: So first and foremost, everything we do is novel, right?
sentences.zh: 首先也是最重要的，我们做的一切都是新颖的，对吧？

sentences.en: It's different than any other format.
sentences.zh: 它不同于任何其他形式。

sentences.en: We're not inviting people over for a casino themed fundraiser or for a steak dinner or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我们不是邀请人们来参加赌场主题的筹款活动，也不是来吃牛排晚餐之类的。

sentences.en: We're fundamentally inviting them over for an experience that they can't have anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 我们本质上是邀请他们来体验一种他们在别处无法获得的经历。

sentences.en: And so I think that there's a whole collection of people who are drawn in by novelty.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有一大群人是被新奇感吸引进来的。

sentences.en: The second characteristic is curation, right?
sentences.zh: 第二个特点是精心策划，对吧？

sentences.en: If you look at the really influential people in the world, they're willing to spend a fortune to enter the right rooMs.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看世界上那些真正有影响力的人，他们愿意花大钱去进入正确的圈子。

sentences.en: And so you look at Davos, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你看达沃斯论坛，对吧？

sentences.en: It's $250,000 or something to attend a freezing conference where you stand in the snow or slush of Davos hoping to bump into Andrea Merkel's, right?
sentences.zh: 花25万美元左右去参加一个冻僵的会议，站在达沃斯的雪地或泥泞中，希望能偶遇安格拉·默克尔之类的人，对吧？

sentences.en: And so if you can curate an environment with interesting people, especially from diverse backgrounds, then that becomes novel and interesting.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你能营造一个汇聚有趣人物的环境，尤其是来自不同背景的人，那么这就变得新颖且有趣了。

sentences.en: Now, I don't know if people are coming thinking that they can get a business deal.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不知道人们来这里是不是觉得能谈成一笔生意。

sentences.en: I think it's more because, frankly, like, you know, I'm the one inviting everybody and I can do business with less than, I don't know, maybe 3% of the people.
sentences.zh: 我认为更多是因为，坦率地说，你知道的，我是发出邀请的人，而我能和不到——我不知道，也许不到百分之三的人——做成生意。

sentences.en: Like, I have no business to be done with Olympic medalists or Nobel laureates.
sentences.zh: 比如，我和奥运奖牌得主或诺贝尔奖得主之间根本没有生意可做。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just a completely different world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这完全是两个不同的世界。

sentences.en: And so then I also think some people come because it's just a fundamentally generous experience.
sentences.zh: 所以我也认为有些人来是因为这本质上是一次慷慨的体验。

sentences.en: Most people are of the, at that level, everybody's after something from them.
sentences.zh: 大多数人，在这个层面上，每个人都想从他们身上得到些什么。

sentences.en: And so I, since I have no angle, then I think that they're coming for that as well.
sentences.zh: 既然我没有功利目的，那么我想他们也是冲着这一点来的。

sentences.en: But, uh, so I think that's the starting point.
sentences.zh: 但是，呃，所以我觉得这是起点。

sentences.en: Now, what we also do digitally is really different than what we do in person.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们在数字端所做的事情与我们在现场所做的事情有很大不同。

sentences.en: And we found that for digital events right now, everybody's been doing a lift and shift.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，对于目前的线上活动，每个人都在搞“复制粘贴”。

sentences.en: They just take their in-person programming and make a much junkier, worse version of it online.
sentences.zh: 他们只是把线下的节目搬到网上，做一个粗制滥造、糟糕得多的版本。

sentences.en: And so you end up on like an 800 person Webex feeling like you don't matter.
sentences.zh: 结果你参加了一个有800人的Webex会议，感觉自己无足轻重。

sentences.en: And so we try to make everything completely interactive and spend as much time as possible in breakout rooms, playing games together and connecting.
sentences.zh: 所以我们尽量让一切完全互动，并花尽可能多的时间在分组会议室里，一起玩游戏和交流。

sentences.en: And the games really function as a social catalyst, both for them to get to know each other.
sentences.zh: 游戏确实起到了社交催化剂的作用，既能让他们互相了解，

sentences.en: And, uh, Jillian, my hunch is you have tons of ideas on this and also function as a great way to reduce stress because that pro-social behavior of play, uh,
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，吉莉安，我猜你在这方面有很多想法，它也是减轻压力的绝佳方式，因为这种游戏的亲社会行为，呃，

sentences.en: when we're all so anxious and wound up these days, I think is really effective at it.
sentences.zh: 当我们在这些日子里都如此焦虑和紧绷时，我认为这在这方面真的很有效。

sentences.en: Um, I love what you're saying about not having an angle, like feeling like the people that you're talking to are not trying to get something from you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我非常喜欢你所说的没有功利目的，就像感觉你交谈的人并不是想从你身上得到什么一样。

sentences.en: And that kind of connects to what I said earlier about, you know, what I think is happening if I talk to someone on the bus.
sentences.zh: 这与我之前说的有点联系，关于如果我和公交车上的人说话，我以为会发生什么。

sentences.en: And I think that there is that stage where they worry that I am trying to get something from them.
sentences.zh: 我认为确实有这样一个阶段，他们会担心我是想从他们那里得到什么。

sentences.en: But it's also something I think about in terms of networking, you know, because I've done a lot of work on how to talk to strangers and I've run these,
sentences.zh: 但这也是我在考虑人际交往时会想到的事情，因为我做过很多关于如何与陌生人交谈的研究，而且我开办过这些——

sentences.en: how to talk to strangers workshops.
sentences.zh: 如何与陌生人交谈的工作坊。

sentences.en: I've been approached to help people with networking and I'm like, I don't teach networking.
sentences.zh: 有人找我帮忙做社交网络培训，而我说，我不教社交网络。

sentences.en: I mean, you can't network without talking to people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不和别人说话，你怎么建立人脉呢？

sentences.en: So in that sense, it is connected, right?
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，它们是相通的，对吧？

sentences.en: And I'll definitely help happy to help you, you know, train people on how to talk to each other.
sentences.zh: 我绝对很乐意帮你，你知道的，培训人们如何互相交谈。

sentences.en: But I think lots of good things come even when you don't have an intention to get something.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，即使你没有获得什么的目的，很多美好的事情也会发生。

sentences.en: And I think the reason networking can feel a little icky is because it feels very instrumental.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人际交往有时会让人觉得有点讨人厌，是因为它感觉太具功利性了。

sentences.en: It feels like you're doing it for a purpose.
sentences.zh: 感觉你这么做是有目的的。

sentences.en: And so people are sort of focused on the purpose rather than just focused on connecting.
sentences.zh: 所以人们把焦点放在了目的上，而不是仅仅专注于建立连接。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, I think when it's just you're doing it for enjoyment and I definitely agree that it can often be a very pro-social thing to talk to other people as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我想当你纯粹是为了享受乐趣而做这件事时——我绝对同意，与他人交谈通常也是一种非常亲社会的行为。

sentences.en: That those motives can result in other outcomes.
sentences.zh: 这些动机可以带来其他结果。

sentences.en: But I think it goes more smoothly when you don't enter a conversation with that purpose.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，如果你带着那种目的进入对话，事情就不会那么顺利。

sentences.en: I love that you called networking icky because I'm in complete agreement.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你把人际交往称为“讨人厌”，因为我完全赞同。

sentences.en: I think it stinks.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Research by Francesca Gino from Harvard Business School looked at the association to networking and found that people feel the need to wash because they feel so dirty from the experience.
sentences.zh: 哈佛商学院的弗兰西斯卡·吉诺（Francesca Gino）的一项研究考察了人们对人际交往的联想，发现人们觉得自己需要洗手，因为这段经历让他们感觉太肮脏了。

sentences.en: And so my hunch is that we're probably on a similar page in terms of my objective is not for anybody to network because that feels very unnatural, but for people to make friends.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜我们在这方面有共识，我的目标不是让任何人去搞什么人际交往，因为那感觉很不自然，而是让人们交朋友。

sentences.en: Because everybody wants great friends, but nobody wants to feel like they're using some.
sentences.zh: 因为每个人都想要好朋友，但没有人愿意觉得自己是在被别人利用。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe a handful of people do, but most of the people I want to interact with aren't interested in that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许少数人愿意，但我想要互动的绝大多数人对那不感兴趣。

sentences.en: So, Jillian, how do you teach people to talk to strangers?
sentences.zh: 所以，吉莉安，你如何教人们与陌生人交谈？

sentences.en: How do you get started?
sentences.zh: 你是如何开始的？

sentences.en: Well, so I run these how to talk to strangers workshops and I treat it as I'm not – I try not to teach.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我开设了这些“如何与陌生人交谈”的工作坊，我把它当作——我尽量不去“教”。

sentences.en: I'm rather just facilitating because I think a lot of times people already know what to do.
sentences.zh: 我其实只是在引导，因为我觉得很多时候人们已经知道该怎么做了。

sentences.en: They just feel like they don't.
sentences.zh: 他们只是觉得自己不知道。

sentences.en: Like they sort of build it up in their head as something that's really hard.
sentences.zh: 就像他们在脑海里把这想象成一件非常困难的事情。

sentences.en: But for example, starting a conversation – I mean, I've run this workshop, you know, not so many times, but, you know, half a dozen times at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 但举个例子，开启一段对话——我的意思是，我举办过这个工作坊，你知道的，虽然不多，但至少也有六七次了。

sentences.en: And people never have trouble coming up with dozens of ways to start a conversation.
sentences.zh: 人们在想出几十种开启对话的方法时从来没有遇到过困难。

sentences.en: So people know what to do.
sentences.zh: 所以人们知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: They just feel like maybe they're doing the wrong thing or maybe they should be doing something else.
sentences.zh: 他们只是觉得自己可能做错了，或者应该做点别的。

sentences.en: Maybe there's something better.
sentences.zh: 也许有更好的选择。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I think it's mostly about helping people realize that it's not just them who feels nervous and awkward about talking to strangers.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为这主要是为了帮助人们意识到，不仅是他们自己跟陌生人说话时会感到紧张和尴尬。

sentences.en: It is a common thing.
sentences.zh: 这很常见。

sentences.en: So I think what I've heard as feedback from these workshops is that that's often the biggest takeaway for people that just by talking to each other,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，从这些工作坊收到的反馈来看，这往往是人们最大的收获，只要通过互相交流，

sentences.en: because I use breakout rooms a lot, like what John was saying, like putting people into it and getting them to talk to each other and share their experiences.
sentences.zh: 因为我经常使用分组讨论室，就像约翰刚才说的，把大家分到小组里，让他们互相交流并分享各自的经历。

sentences.en: People really walk away realizing it's not just them and that other people are worried about the same things and that, you know,
sentences.zh: 人们离开时真的会意识到，不仅自己如此，别人也在担心同样的事情，而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: we can just be a little braver knowing that other people are acting the way they are because they feel nervous too.
sentences.zh: 只要知道别人表现成那样也是因为他们同样感到紧张，我们就能稍微勇敢一点。

sentences.en: It's not that they don't want to connect.
sentences.zh: 并不是他们不想建立联系。

sentences.en: It's just that they're worried about the same things that you are.
sentences.zh: 只是他们和你一样担心着同样的事情。

sentences.en: So just a lot of reflection, I guess, to answer your question is how do I teach people is just I get people to think about, OK, how can you start a conversation?
sentences.zh: 所以，为了回答你的问题，我教大家的方法其实就是引导大家反思，让他们去思考：好吧，你该如何开始一段对话？

sentences.en: What is your worst fear?
sentences.zh: 你最大的恐惧是什么？

sentences.en: Like, what do you think could go wrong?
sentences.zh: 比如，你觉得可能会出什么问题？

sentences.en: And then maybe think about, well, what could you do if that thing actually happened, which it probably won't.
sentences.zh: 然后不妨想一想，如果那件事真的发生了——虽然大概率不会发生——你又能做些什么。

sentences.en: Um, and then especially talk about rejection, because that is a big concern.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特别是要谈谈被拒绝这件事，因为这是一个很大的顾虑。

sentences.en: So I talk about I get people to think about what does rejection look like?
sentences.zh: 所以我跟他们探讨，引导大家思考：被拒绝到底是什么样子的？

sentences.en: Like, how, how do we decide to interpret something as rejection?
sentences.zh: 比如，我们是怎么决定把某种情况解释为拒绝的？

sentences.en: And then how could we, you know, thinking about those things like people not making eye contact or looking at their phone or looking at their watch or, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后我们该如何看待这些情况，比如别人不和我们对视、看手机、看手表，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: making some physical space and say, well, what else could be going on?
sentences.zh: 拉开一些物理距离，然后想想：还可能会发生什么？

sentences.en: Could it be something other than a personal rejection and people at first to have a bit of trouble coming up with other alternative explanations?
sentences.zh: 会不会是除了个人拒绝之外的其他原因呢？人们一开始很难想出其他替代解释。

sentences.en: But then once you get the ball rolling, people can quickly see, well, maybe that person doesn't speak English and is having trouble understanding me.
sentences.zh: 但一旦打开了思路，大家很快就会明白：也许那个人不会说英语，正在努力理解我的意思。

sentences.en: Or maybe they're worried they had a bad day at work.
sentences.zh: 或者也许他们正心事重重，今天工作不顺。

sentences.en: Or maybe they're waiting for they really are waiting for a phone call because their dog is at the vet or, you know, like there's a lot of things that could be going on.
sentences.zh: 或者也许他们在等——是真的在等一个电话，因为他们的狗在兽医那儿，或者，你知道的，可能会有很多种原因。

sentences.en: And so the tricky thing about having a conversation is, of course, you can't read other people's minds.
sentences.zh: 所以，进行对话棘手的地方在于，你当然无法读懂别人的心思。

sentences.en: And so what we do is we we somehow have this negative voice in our head and we invent all these stories about what's going on in the other person's mind.
sentences.zh: 因此我们所做的就是，脑海中总会有个消极的声音，编造出各种关于对方心里在想什么的剧情。

sentences.en: But most of that is not true.
sentences.zh: 但其中大部分都不是真的。

sentences.en: You know, so I've done work on something called the liking gap, which is the fact that when you finish having a conversation with someone who's new,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我曾就所谓“喜爱差距”进行过研究，事实就是，当你和新认识的人结束谈话后，

sentences.en: we tend to think that the other person didn't like us as much as we liked them.
sentences.zh: 我们往往会觉得对方并没有像我们喜欢他们那样喜欢我们。

sentences.en: And it's just not correct.
sentences.zh: 而这其实是不对的。

sentences.en: So we so again, it's just another example of how we worry more than we should.
sentences.zh: 所以——再次说明，这只是又一个例子，证明了我们的担忧远远超过了应有的程度。

sentences.en: And like I said, it's because we can't read other people's minds.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，这是因为我们无法读懂别人的心思。

sentences.en: So I think that really resonates with people and maybe helps people feel a little braver that, you know, if they if if you can convince people, actually,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这真的能引起大家的共鸣，或许能让人们觉得勇敢一点，你知道的，如果你能让人相信，事实上，

sentences.en: it's not as bad as you think.
sentences.zh: 事情并没有你想的那么糟糕。

sentences.en: And people like you more than you think, then people might have a little might be a little braver about starting a conversation.
sentences.zh: 而且人们其实比你想象的更喜欢你，那么大家在主动搭话时或许就会稍微勇敢一些。

sentences.en: What about stopping a conversation?
sentences.zh: 那如何结束一段对话呢？

sentences.en: Do you explain to people how to do that?
sentences.zh: 你会向大家解释怎么做吗？

sentences.en: And I'm thinking because we were talking about networking a little while ago.
sentences.zh: 我想问这个是因为我们不久前刚刚聊到社交网络。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I've always found at networking events is that you go up to somebody, you start talking and then you say, oh,
sentences.zh: 我一直在社交活动中发现的一个现象是，你走过去和某人交谈，然后你会想：哦，

sentences.en: this person isn't going to be any help to me.
sentences.zh: 这个人对我的帮助一点都不大。

sentences.en: And I want this conversation to stop.
sentences.zh: 我可不想再聊下去了。

sentences.en: How can I stop it nicely and get away?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么礼貌地结束对话并脱身呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Well, I definitely do talk about ending a conversation at the how to talk to strangers workshops.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在“如何与陌生人交谈”的工作坊里确实会讲到如何结束对话。

sentences.en: And it is the thing that I find the most difficult.
sentences.zh: 而这恰恰是我发现最困难的事情。

sentences.en: So I said earlier that people can find dozens of ways to start a conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以我刚才说过，人们能找到几十种开始对话的方法。

sentences.en: But ending one, people seem to find a lot harder and mostly people just lie.
sentences.zh: 但要结束对话，大家似乎觉得难得多，而且大多数人只会撒谎。

sentences.en: So they make up an excuse like they, you know, they have to go to the toilet or they need to get a drink or they have to make a phone call or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会编造借口，比如，你知道的，他们得去洗手间，或者需要去喝杯饮料，或者必须打个电话之类的。

sentences.en: And a lot of the time, these are lies.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，这些都是借口。

sentences.en: Sometimes they are true.
sentences.zh: 有时它们确实是真的。

sentences.en: But a lot of times people are just saying this because they just don't know what to say.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候人们这么说，只是因为他们不知道该说些什么。

sentences.en: But every time I run this workshop, at some point, someone will just speak up and say that what they do is just thank the other person for their time and say, it's time to go now.
sentences.zh: 不过每次我办这个工作坊时，总会在某个时刻有人站出来说，他们的做法就是感谢对方抽出时间，然后说：现在该走了。

sentences.en: You know, thank you, but we're done.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，谢谢你，但我们要结束了。

sentences.en: And people kind of look at this person, whoever this one person is, and think, what, you can do that?
sentences.zh: 大家就会看着这个人——无论具体是哪个人——心想：什么，这样也行？

sentences.en: But there's brand new research just published a couple weeks ago from some folks at Harvard and other places looking at ending conversations.
sentences.zh: 但就在几周前，哈佛和其他地方的一些学者刚刚发表了一项全新的研究，专门探讨结束对话的问题。

sentences.en: And they found that basically conversations never end.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，基本上对话从来不会在正确的时间结束。

sentences.en: I think it was 2% of the times a conversation ends at exactly the moment that both people wished it would end.
sentences.zh: 我想只有2%的时候，对话恰好在双方都希望结束的那一刻结束。

sentences.en: So sometimes people talk longer than they wish they would have.
sentences.zh: 所以有时人们聊的时间比自己希望的要长。

sentences.en: Sometimes people talk less time than they would have liked to.
sentences.zh: 有时人们聊的时间比自己想要的要短。

sentences.en: And again, it's this attempt to sort of coordinate with someone else when you can't read their mind.
sentences.zh: 同样，这也是一种试图与他人协调的行为，偏偏你又读不懂对方的心思。

sentences.en: And so you might think that they, you know, that you can't stop talking because that would be impolite.
sentences.zh: 因此你可能会觉得，你知道的，你不能停止聊天，因为那样很不礼貌。

sentences.en: But it seems that the best bet is just to, you know, at the networking event, the example that you're giving is just say, you know, thanks.
sentences.zh: 但最好的办法似乎就是，你知道的，在社交场合中，就像你刚才举的例子，直接说：你知道的，谢谢你。

sentences.en: It's been nice talking to you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴和你聊聊。

sentences.en: We're here to network.
sentences.zh: 我们来这里是为了拓展人脉。

sentences.en: So let's go and do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们去别处转转吧。

sentences.en: I think we can do it in a polite way.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们可以用一种礼貌的方式做到这一点。

sentences.en: I think it's so interesting because my general view is not to go to a networking event and instead find shared activities that actually interest people.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太有趣了，因为我的普遍观点是不要去参加那种纯粹的社交派对，而是去寻找真正能吸引人们的共同活动。

sentences.en: So I'd almost rather go on a hike, right,
sentences.zh: 所以我宁愿去远足，对吧，

sentences.en: with people or start a run club or some kind of board games night and give an excuse to either invite people or join ones that already exiSt.
sentences.zh: 和大家一起，或者发起一个跑步俱乐部、某种桌游之夜，以此为借口去邀请别人，或者加入现有的活动。

sentences.en: So there's like lists and lists and lists and lists of things on Meetup.com or Eventbrite or so on that give us an opportunity to connect with people in a much more natural context than a bunch of overly priced alcohol in a room that has loud music in it.
sentences.zh: 所以在 Meetup.com、Eventbrite 或类似平台上，有无数多这样的活动列表，它们为我们提供了在一个自然得多的语境下与人建立联系的机会，而不是去一个塞满嘈杂音乐、酒水价格虚高的房间里。

sentences.en: Because it just feels like such a lot.
sentences.zh: 因为那种感觉太牵强了。

sentences.en: Because it just feels like such an unnatural environment.
sentences.zh: 因为感觉这就是一个极不自然的环境。

sentences.en: And I used to, when I was in my single days,
sentences.zh: 我过去单身的时候，

sentences.en: I used to explain to people that I'm not a fan of clubs because I'm not so good looking that anybody would want to talk to me at a club because you can't hear the person.
sentences.zh: 我常常跟别人解释说我不喜欢去夜店，因为我长得不够帅，在夜店里没人会想跟我说话，而且里面声音太吵，根本听不清别人说什么。

sentences.en: But I'm much better at a bus stop because I'm decent at having a conversation.
sentences.zh: 但我在公交车站表现得好得多，因为我很擅长聊天。

sentences.en: I think another thing that that taps into, John, is just introversion.
sentences.zh: 我觉得约翰，这也触及了另一个特质，那就是内向。

sentences.en: Like I'm very much an introvert.
sentences.zh: 比如我就是一个非常内向的人。

sentences.en: And I always try to mention that when I talk about this research because I don't want people to walk away thinking, oh, well, it's just, you know,
sentences.zh: 我每次谈到这项研究时总是会提到这一点，因为我不想让大家带着这样的想法离开：哦，好吧，

sentences.en: it's only extroverts that are going to do crazy stuff like talk to a stranger.
sentences.zh: 只有外向的人才会去做跟陌生人说话这种疯狂的事。

sentences.en: I would never want to go to that environment where the music is loud and there's 100 people.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会想去那种音乐震耳欲聋、有一百个人的环境。

sentences.en: Like that's just overwhelming for an introvert like me, which is, you know, a large minority of the population.
sentences.zh: 对像我这样内向的人来说，那简直令人招架不住——而内向者占了人口相当大的少数。

sentences.en: And so these kind of situations that you're describing are much more comfortable for someone like that.
sentences.zh: 所以你所描述的这种场景对这样的人来说要舒适得多。

sentences.en: And I find these kind of one-to-one conversations are just not scary for an introvert.
sentences.zh: 而且我发现这种一对一的对话对内向者来说一点也不可怕。

sentences.en: Like I talk to strangers all the time because it doesn't feel scary to me.
sentences.zh: 就像我经常和陌生人聊天，因为这对我来说并不可怕。

sentences.en: I mean, it's taken some time to get there.
sentences.zh: 我是说，达到这种状态花了一些时间。

sentences.en: It's not something I've done my whole life and there has been some skill building that makes these conversations go better, which makes me feel more comfortable with them.
sentences.zh: 这不是我一辈子都在做的事，期间我也进行了一些技能训练，让这些对话进行得更顺利，这也让我对它们感到更加自适。

sentences.en: But I can walk away.
sentences.zh: 但我随时可以离开。

sentences.en: These are not conversations that are intended to last for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 这些谈话本来就不是为了持续很长时间而设计的。

sentences.en: And so it's very low stakes to me.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这没什么大不了的风险。

sentences.en: And I find that maybe it especially suits an introvert.
sentences.zh: 我发现它可能特别适合内向的人。

sentences.en: John, I'm just wondering, I mean, a lot of what you do to bring people together involves reaching out to strangers.
sentences.zh: 约翰，我在想，我是说，你用来把大家聚在一起的很多事情都涉及主动接触陌生人。

sentences.en: What kinds of reactions do you generally get?
sentences.zh: 你通常会得到什么样的反应？

sentences.en: Oh, I get everything.
sentences.zh: 哦，什么样的都有。

sentences.en: I mean, I have literally gotten, I think the best response saying no was, I don't do blind dates, which I thought was hilarious.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我真的遇到过各种各样的回答，我觉得拒绝得最好的回复是：“我不搞相亲”，这把我逗乐了。

sentences.en: I was like, respect.
sentences.zh: 我当时心想：真酷，佩服。

sentences.en: To speak to what Jillian was pointing to about trying to understand what's going on in another person's head,
sentences.zh: 正如吉莉安刚才所指出的，为了理解别人心里在想什么，

sentences.en: the incredible amount of social anxiety that highly influential people have is, was staggeringly shocking to me.
sentences.zh: 那些极具影响力的人所承受的巨大社交焦虑，让我感到震惊得难以置信。

sentences.en: Like unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 简直不可思议。

sentences.en: I mean, famous directors, actors, musicians, like all of it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，著名的导演、演员、音乐家，全都有这种感觉。

sentences.en: But I've even had an actor say to me, I know how to be anybody but myself.
sentences.zh: 甚至有一个演员对我说：“除了做自己，我知道怎么扮演任何人。”

sentences.en: And so when I'm me, I'm awkward.
sentences.zh: “所以当我是我自己的时候，我很尴尬。”

sentences.en: And this is somebody that you would know by name.
sentences.zh: 而这是一个你叫得出名字的人。

sentences.en: You've seen this person in film and on television.
sentences.zh: 你在电影和电视里都见过这个人。

sentences.en: And, uh, and I think that there's this misperception often of other people's social capability because you think that they're successful or impressive.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，我认为人们常常对别人的社交能力存在这种误解，因为你觉得他们很成功、很令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: Um, and so the, the most odd one I've ever gotten, most odd response was actually from a famous psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，我遇到过最奇怪的、最奇怪的反应其实来自于一位著名的心理学家。

sentences.en: I'm not going to say who it was, uh, but you absolutely know who this person is.
sentences.zh: 我不会说那是谁，嗯，但你绝对知道这个人是谁。

sentences.en: Um, and the response was, uh, something to the extent of how dare you invite, expect me to pay for a dinner where I'm usually the person who's honored at the dinner.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他的反应是，大致意思是：你怎么敢邀请、指望我为一个晚餐买单，我通常才是晚餐上受表彰的那个人。

sentences.en: Um, and we responded very politely and we were like, I don't know what made you even think that there's a fee we pay for everything.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们非常礼貌地回复了，我们说：不知道是什么让你觉得有这回事，我们承担所有费用。

sentences.en: And everybody in attendance is, you know, very successful and interesting and so on.
sentences.zh: 而且出席的每个人，你知道的，都非常成功、有趣等等。

sentences.en: And unsurprisingly, we never got a response back, but, uh, it's, it's, uh, it took us a really long time to figure out.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，我们再也没有收到回复，但是，嗯，这，我们花了很长时间才摸索出来，

sentences.en: Um, what to put into the emails, what frequently asked questions, how frankly, not to sound, um, overly exclusive.
sentences.zh: 嗯，邮件里该写什么，常见问题解答有哪些，坦率地说，怎么才能显得不那么，嗯，过于排外。

sentences.en: So we work really hard to curate, but we are not like a nightclub.
sentences.zh: 所以我们非常努力地进行筛选，但我们不是夜店。

sentences.en: We're not trying to keep people out just for the sake of seeming cool.
sentences.zh: 我们不是为了显得很酷而故意把人拒之门外。

sentences.en: It's just that I can't afford to pay for millions of people's meals.
sentences.zh: 只是我承担不起为几百万人的饭局买单的费用。

sentences.en: Uh, so we kind of keep it small.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们把规模控制得比较小。

sentences.en: And then we also launched a salon series that's more open to the public.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还推出了一个对公众更加开放的沙龙系列。

sentences.en: If kind of people just message me, we're often happy to just host them.
sentences.zh: 如果有人直接给我发消息，我们通常都很乐意接待他们。

sentences.en: And we have a nonprofit arm that just runs programming for the public.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一个非营利机构，专门为公众开展活动项目。

sentences.en: So we try to really be inclusive of everybody, but the responses we get are kind of just hilarious at times.
sentences.zh: 所以我们努力做到真正包容所有人，但我们收到的回复有时确实挺搞笑的。

sentences.en: So Jillian, what, what research are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 那么吉莉安，你现在在做什么研究？

sentences.en: What are your next, the next questions that you want to answer?
sentences.zh: 你接下来想要解答的问题是什么？

sentences.en: Well, it occurred to me one day that I've been studying these, you know, conversations with strangers are, are in some sense, a difficult conversation for many people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我有一天突然意识到，我一直在研究的这些，你知道的，与陌生人的对话，在某种意义上对许多人来说都是一场艰难的对话。

sentences.en: People find it a difficult thing.
sentences.zh: 人们发现这是一件很难的事情。

sentences.en: And I was talking earlier about all the different fears that people have.
sentences.zh: 我刚才也谈到了人们心里的各种恐惧。

sentences.en: And it occurred to me one day that there's other kinds of conversations that might have, might involve similar fears.
sentences.zh: 我有一天突然想到，还有其他种类的对话可能也会涉及类似的恐惧。

sentences.en: So I'm thinking of things like talking to someone that, you know, who's just, uh, lost their partner or someone who's had a miscarriage or someone who's been diagnosed with cancer.
sentences.zh: 所以我想到了比如和这样的人说话：你知道的，刚失去伴侣的人，或者经历过流产的人，或者被诊断出癌症的人。

sentences.en: And so I just got really curious about whether there's kind of a common set of fears that people might have,
sentences.zh: 所以我开始对人们内心是否存在一组共同的恐惧感到非常好奇，

sentences.en: if maybe the fears that people have about talking to strangers might be similar to the fears that people have in these other kinds of conversations.
sentences.zh: 也许人们在与陌生人交谈时感到的恐惧，可能与人们在其他这些类型的对话中所感到的恐惧相似。

sentences.en: Um, so that, that's what I'm studying right now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，这就是我目前正在研究的内容。

sentences.en: And I have an ongoing study that I'd love some help with.
sentences.zh: 我有一项正在进行的研究，非常希望能得到一些帮助。

sentences.en: So anybody who wants to check out my website at JillianSandstrom.com, if you've experienced one of these things, cancer diagnosis, miscarriage, or bereavement, um,
sentences.zh: 所以任何想浏览我网站 JillianSandstrom.com 的人，如果你最近经历过这些事情中的一件——癌症诊断、流产或亲人离世，

sentences.en: relatively recently, and want to talk about what people have said to you in an attempt to be supportive, I would love to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 并且想聊聊别人为了表示支持而对你说过的话，我很希望能听到你的分享。

sentences.en: We'll make sure to put that link in the program notes.
sentences.zh: 我们一定会把这个链接放在节目简介里。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And John, what about you?
sentences.zh: 那约翰你呢？

sentences.en: What's your next project?
sentences.zh: 你的下一个项目是什么？

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Well, so I have the book coming out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我有本书要出版了。

sentences.en: Uh, you're invited, the art and science of cultivating influence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，《承蒙邀请：培养影响力的艺术与科学》（You're Invited: The Art and Science of Cultivating Influence）。

sentences.en: And I think that my biggest focus is finding a whole collection of ways to just help people come together.
sentences.zh: 我想我最大的重点是寻找一整套方法来帮助人们聚在一起。

sentences.en: So whether it's wild pop-ups in New York that I get people to volunteer to run and do activities in public at safe distances now that summer's coming,
sentences.zh: 所以，无论是在纽约举办的疯狂快闪活动，我让大家自愿参与，在夏天即将到来、保持安全距离的前提下在公共场所开展活动，

sentences.en: or it's online experiences and events that we can just disseminate so that people can have this, these conversations, whether it's with strangers or with their family reunions.
sentences.zh: 还是我们在网上推广的体验和活动，好让人们能够进行这些对话，无论是与陌生人还是在家族聚会上。

sentences.en: Because right now everybody's doing like happy hours.
sentences.zh: 因为现在每个人都在搞什么欢乐时光（happy hour）。

sentences.en: And I'll be honest, I'm, I'm not a huge fan of promoting drinking when you're stressed.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我，我其实不是很支持在压力大的时候提倡喝酒。

sentences.en: Uh, it's, I don't think it's like the, the social cues that are, are the best for us.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得这并不是，那种传递出来的社交信号对我们来说是最好的。

sentences.en: And also by the third time your company runs the happy hour, you're like, okay, we're going to have the same conversation, the same, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且当你的公司第三次举办欢乐时光时，你会想：好吧，我们要进行同样的对话，同样的，你知道的，

sentences.en: extroverts are going to take over the conversation.
sentences.zh: 外向的人会掌控整个对话。

sentences.en: I'm going to stay quiet, turn the camera off, wash my dishes and feel like, okay, I've shown up, so I'm not going to get in trouble.
sentences.zh: 我要保持安静，关掉摄像头，去洗碗，然后觉得自己：好吧，我露面了，所以不会惹上麻烦。

sentences.en: But if we could give people activities, conversations to have, uh, games, maybe ways to even include their kids.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们能给人们提供活动、可以展开的对话、游戏，甚至可能是把孩子们也包含进来的方式，

sentences.en: So people kind of get to know the extended family, right?
sentences.zh: 好让大家有机会了解彼此的大家庭，对吧？

sentences.en: Right now we're not having the hallway conversations, the water cooler conversations that reduce anxiety and give us a peek into people's lives,
sentences.zh: 现在我们没有了那种能缓解焦虑、让我们一窥他人生活的走廊对话、茶水间闲聊，

sentences.en: but we're actually seeing directly into their homes.
sentences.zh: 但我们实际上是直接看到了彼此的家中。

sentences.en: Maybe we could use this as an opportunity to really get to know each other.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以借此机会真正了解彼此。

sentences.en: And so, uh, that's the kind of stuff I'm exploring, but, uh, and then I have a really big mission, which is, uh,
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，这就是我在探索的那类东西，不过，呃，然后我有一个非常重大的使命，那就是，呃，

sentences.en: I find that most of the sales processes that companies go through are like a huge waste of money.
sentences.zh: 我发现公司经历的大多数销售流程就像是极大的资金浪费。

sentences.en: Um, and a lot of the marketing budgets are really wasted because they don't create a meaningful relationship between the company and people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，许多营销预算其实都被浪费了，因为它们没有在公司和人们之间建立起有意义的联系。

sentences.en: And so, uh,
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，

sentences.en: you know, I'm never going to be remembered for anything, but if it is, if I am, it's that I got the most influential people in our culture to come to my home,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我从没想过自己会被任何人记住，但如果要说有的话，那就是我让文化界最具影响力的人来到我家，

sentences.en: cook me dinner, wash my dishes, clean my floors, and then thank me for it.
sentences.zh: 给我做饭、洗碗、打扫地板，然后还要为此感谢我。

sentences.en: And if I can do that with no budget, then companies are spending way too much trying to connect with their customers.
sentences.zh: 如果我能在零预算的情况下做到这一点，那么各大公司为了与客户建立联系而花费的资金就实在太多了。

sentences.en: And so if we can create actual sense of community or belonging or connection, and it doesn't need to cost a lot, maybe we could shift the entire marketing world.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们能营造出真正的社区感、归属感或连接感，而且不需要花费太多成本，也许我们就能改变整个营销界。

sentences.en: So your aspirations aren't that big then just shifting the entire marketing world.
sentences.zh: 所以你的宏大志向也不过就是改变整个营销界嘛。

sentences.en: Marketing world.
sentences.zh: 营销界。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, always aim high, right?
sentences.zh: 人总是要志存高远，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you both for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我要感谢你们两今天来参加节目。

sentences.en: Um, I don't know about you, but I'd certainly feel happier and healthier having spoken to you both.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道你们怎么想，但和你们俩交谈过后，我确实感觉更快乐、更健康了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: This is such a treat.
sentences.zh: 这真是一种享受。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you, John.
sentences.zh: 很高兴认识你，约翰。

sentences.en: Jillian, you're awesome.
sentences.zh: 吉莉安，你太棒了。

sentences.en: And I look forward to speaking to more strangers.
sentences.zh: 我期待着与更多陌生人交谈。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, you can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology at www.speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或在 Apple、Stitcher 以及其他收听播客的地方找到《心理学话题》往期的节目。

sentences.en: And please leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 请给我们留个好评。

sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，请发电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 即 speakingofpsychology，所有字母连在一起，@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 《心理学话题》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.zh: 我们的音响剪辑师是克里斯·孔达扬。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 代表美国心理学协会，我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: And I'm sorry about the bird.
sentences.zh: 真对不起刚才那只鸟。

sentences.en: I hope they can get him out of the recording.
sentences.zh: 希望他们能把它从录音里弄出去。

sentences.en: Are you kidding?
sentences.zh: 你在开玩笑吧？

sentences.en: That's my favorite part.
sentences.zh: 那可是我最喜欢的部分。
